rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Card Types 4 Game End Overview Collect the most points from Golems, Runes, and Gems by game's end Turn On your turn, you have two options If you have 1 or fewer gems, you may take 2 more gems, then your turn ends Alternatively, take a card from the display which has an effect depending on how many other cards still remain in the same row If before taking a card, that row has 3 cards (i.e. it was full) you must place a gem on each other card in that row If before taking a card, that row has 2 cards, transfer the gem from the card you took onto the card you did not take If the card you wish to take is the last in the row, as well as taking the card you gain all the gems on it After you've paid for and taken the card, trigger its ability Card Types There are 3 card types, each with 2 abilities When you take a card, you can trigger only ONE of its possible abilities The types in short are: Golem - Resource & Summon Rune - Resource & Reserve Gem - Reward & Dust Golems can be turned into a Resource, by turning the card upsidedown to show the resource symbol, then place it in a staggered column of the resource type to show how many you have Golems can be Summoned by meeting, but not paying, the resource requirements shown. After which, you must tuck 1-3 resource cards matching the golem requirements underneath, scoring a point for each Runes can be turned into a Resource, similar to golems, except they cannot start a new column, they must be played into pre-existing columns of their resource type (some Runes have wild resource icon, that can be any type) Runes can be Reserved, if you have at least 3 gems, spend 1 gem, and take it into your hand for potential scoring opportunities Gems can give a Reward, collect all gems showing, first from the supply, then from your opponent if not enough, before keeping the card in your hand Gems can be turned to Dust, by turning the card upsidedown to show the quantity of dust supplied, place this in a staggered column of dust for potential scoring opportunities Game End If at the end of a player's turn, you try to fill a row back to 3 cards and there are not enough to fill it, this triggers the end game Make sure everyone has had an equal number of turns, then proceed to scoring 2VP per Summoned Golem 1VP per tucked card under Golems 1/3/6/10VP for 1/2/3/4 Dust (one set only, no points for 5+ Dust) Hand Gems score their depicted VP Hand Runes score their depicted VP The player with the most points, wins! If tied, the player with the most Golems, wins! If still tied, the player with the most Tucked Cards, wins!

---

[Rating: 1/10] It seems to be a cute game, but I can't really tell because of the deficient rulebook.  The rulebook is missing some key info and ambiguous in some key places.  The printer rules are not enough to sit down and play (without a lot of guesswork).  BGG forum and videos help, but I consider that pretty unacceptable.

[Rating: 2/10] Played solo and 2P. We despise the iconography : runes have impossible to decipher tiny sets of symbols. Constantly requires the rulebook. Rulebook is badly written. Game sold.

[Rating: 2/10] Bad art, bad rules, nothing theme. Dry gameplay that doesn't really evolve or ever do anything interesting or challenging. Feels like a poor combination of other mechanics that you can find in other games that deliver a better whole product.

[Rating: 3/10] RULEBOOK: Absolutely terrible. Like in the top 3 worst rulebooks I've ever read.  SOLO: After 5 games, I'm not even close to a win. I might like that, since I enjoy a challenge, but I saw the designer say somewhere that his win rate is 20-30%, assuming you get the rules right. I'm not at all certain I have the rules right, but I know I've got them as right as I can get them. I'm going to say this solo mode is a waste of my time and money. Though I believe this game was actually intended more as a two-player.  MULTIPLAYER: Haven't tried yet. Not sure if I will, but maybe since it's short.

[Rating: 3/10] I've tried to play this a number of times, but for me it's just a swing and a miss. It looks great, and I really want to like it, but I just can't.  It never feels like it goes anywhere, like you're building up a cool army to battle the other person, and then...nothing, the game is over, whoever has the most points wins.  I'm not sure it's a game I'll keep. Maybe if it's the only game I dislike out of the rest of this thunderglyph set, I might just keep it for completsions sake (it's not a big box and it looks cool), but I might get rid of it if there are others that don't mesh as well.

[Rating: 3/10] Rob's game.   I barely remember playing this game. The rulebook was awful and didn't really explain how to play the game.

[Rating: 3.5/10] As with most of the Matchbox Collection, unable to play a satisfying game due to constant questions / issues with the rulebook.  Spent 2 hours trying to figure out how to play a 20 minute game.  A hallmark disappointment from Kickstarter.

[Rating: 3.5/10] Very hard to distinguish symbols, bad rulebook, no expansion rulebook and the expansion cards are hard to distinguish. Too clunky for a light game

[Rating: 4/10] Rulebook is completely broken and awful. Turns out there is a “fixed” rulebook online, still has massive issues. Had to get the FAQ from the forum to even begin to understand how certain cards worked.

[Rating: 4/10] We're not a fan of Golems. It's a mish mash of other games mechanics so it isn't original. The rules are terrible (even in their corrected state). The components/gems are ok. I like the matchbox. The art is awful. There are better games out there I'd rather play.??
